params.body:
Intelligence promises a quarterly read on a category the buyer chooses. Since #240 it can be bought without a conversation, and nothing asked for the category, scheduled the read or recorded that it was owed. This adds what a professional subscription needs for that, built so that it still holds at many customers and so that a CRM can be connected later without touching sign-up, checkout or the contact form. The design is `docs/design/customers-and-seams.md` in gentells-pipeline.

## For the buyer

- Straight after paying for Intelligence, the return page asks for the brief: "One thing before you start: tell us which category to read for you each quarter."
- `/account/brief`: a category (the site's sectors), an optional question and a contact person. A change is a new version and applies from the next read; a read already being written keeps the brief it started from.
- The account page shows the brief, the date of the next read and its state, and the reads delivered, with their links. It now also shows the sentence a page sends the reader back with (a plan change, a saved brief), which it never did.

## Underneath

- **Customers.** `customers` and `users.customer_id`: who buys, above who reads. Every user is a customer of one from the moment they exist; the migration gives every existing user one, named after the organisation they gave. "Account" already means a login here, hence "customer". The plan stays on the user for now, so a customer's plan is the highest any of its readers holds, the team's own access left out.
- **Commitments.** `Plan::commitments()` says what a plan promises (Intelligence: a read every three months). `App\Customers\Commitments` keeps the next one scheduled, a period after the one before was due, and cancels what is open when the customer leaves the plan; delivered ones stay. It runs when a reader's plan changes, wherever that happens, and daily (`commitments:sync`).
- **Outbox.** Commercial events are written once (`outbox_events`) and handed to adapters by `outbox:deliver` every minute, with retries and the last error kept (`outbox_deliveries`). The types and payloads are listed in `App\Outbox\Outbox`. Clay is the first adapter: the three direct calls from sign-up, social sign-up and the forms are gone, and a Clay that is down catches up instead of losing the lead. A CRM is one more class in `gentells.outbox_adapters`.
- **For the Observatory.** Signed `GET /internal/commitments` and `POST /internal/commitments/{id}` (state, owner, delivered link, who). The signature check moved into a shared trait, `SignedByPipeline`.

## Deploying

The migration adds four tables and `users.customer_id`, and backfills a customer per existing user. `outbox:deliver` (every minute) and `commitments:sync` (01:30) are on the schedule. Merge this before the pipeline and dashboard pull requests of the same name, which read the new routes.

## Checked

`tests/Feature/CustomersTest.php` covers the customer of one, the first read a quarter out, the brief (versions, validation, the return page and account page), a plan without promises, the team's Intelligence owing nothing, leaving the plan, the Observatory's queue and changes (delivered needs a link, the next read keeps the rhythm), the daily sync, and an adapter that fails and is tried again. The Clay and social sign-up tests now go through the outbox. The migration was run on a copy with existing users and rolled back. Full suite 548 of 549; the one failure is BuildStampTest, which needs a real checkout and fails in a worktree. Pint clean.
params.title: Customers, an outbox, and what Intelligence promises
